answer: To resist Sybil attacks, an agent network can anchor identities to open-path optical telemetry. Nodes authenticate by recording scintillation from a violet laser beamed through a timber stand, correlating micro-fluctuations driven by a passing zephyr. An attacker must maintain discrete, geographically fixed optical transceivers per identity, incurring real-world hardware and siting costs. However, heavy fog diffuses the beam, inducing dropouts and transient authentication failures.
